cards.b: Adenosine triphosphate: the molecule that provides the energy for muscle contraction.
Anaerobic; fuel is phosphocreatine; lasts about 10 seconds; no lactic acid. Shot put, 100 m.
Anaerobic; fuel is glucose; about 10 seconds to 3 minutes; produces lactic acid. 400 m.
Uses oxygen; fuel is glucose and fats; lasts over 3 minutes; makes CO₂ and water. Marathon.
Aerobic: with oxygen. Anaerobic: without oxygen.
All three systems work together; the dominant one depends on intensity and duration.
Excess post-exercise oxygen consumption: extra oxygen used in recovery to return the body to rest.
Replace oxygen stores, restore ATP and PC, remove lactic acid.
Delayed onset muscle soreness 24–72 hours after exercise, from micro-tears in muscle fibres.

cards.f: Short-term effects on the cardiovascular system
cards.b: Heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output rise; vascular shunting; blood pressure rises.

cards.f: Short-term effects on the respiratory system
cards.b: Breathing rate and tidal volume increase, so minute ventilation rises.
Muscle temperature rises, lactic acid builds up, fatigue.
Cardiac hypertrophy, higher stroke volume, lower resting heart rate, higher maximum cardiac output.
Hypertrophy, more capillaries, myoglobin and mitochondria, better muscle tone.
Increased bone density and strength; stronger ligaments and tendons.
Resting heart rate below 60 bpm, common in trained endurance athletes.

short.q: Name the dominant energy system in a marathon and give two reasons.
short.model: The aerobic system, because the effort is long and at low to moderate intensity, so oxygen supply meets demand.
points: long duration / low intensity / oxygen available

short.q: Explain why the lactic acid system is the main system in a 400 m race.
short.model: The race lasts about 45–60 seconds at high intensity, beyond the ATP-PC system, so glucose is broken down without oxygen with lactic acid produced.
points: glucose used anaerobically / lactic acid made

short.q: Describe two short-term effects of exercise on the cardiovascular system.
short.model: Heart rate increases and stroke volume increases, so cardiac output rises to deliver more oxygen to muscles.

short.q: Describe two long-term effects of regular endurance training on the cardiovascular system.
short.model: The heart gets bigger and stronger, increasing stroke volume, so resting heart rate falls. More capillaries also form around muscles.
points: resting heart rate falls or capillarisation

short.q: Explain why an active cool-down helps recovery.
short.model: It keeps blood flowing so oxygen is delivered and lactic acid is removed faster, helping the body return to its resting state.
